title: Rosalind and the Glasshouse
premise: Astrid Vasquez, a night librarian in a city that never quite sleeps anymore, has spent twelve years orbiting her closest friend Theo without ever saying what she feels. When Ilan Reyes, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, asks her to become his final student before his memory fails entirely, she accepts — and discovers that the language carries the history of the old glasshouse neighborhood where she grew up and from which her family was displaced. As rerouting of the last bus line threatens to sever the neighborhood forever, Astrid must transcribe a vanishing tongue, confront the stranger in her grandmother's old photographs — a woman who chose duty over love — and finally choose differently herself. The book ends with Ilan's death, the language living on in one new voice, and Astrid boarding the final bus with Theo, having said it at last.
about_author: Tamsin Halloran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in coastal cities before turning to fiction. She writes about inheritance, quiet love, and the places we lose to timetables.

chapters.title: The Hours Between Buses
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet the night library, its insomniac regulars, and Theo, who brings her coffee every shift without being asked. Their almost-conversation is interrupted by closing announcements. Emotional beat: tenderness practiced into habit, love deferred so long it looks like friendship.

chapters.title: A Man Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Ilan Reyes arrives at the reference desk at 2 a.m., asking for help finding 'someone to leave things to.' Astrid assumes he means objects. He means words. POV: Astrid. Beat: curiosity kindled; the first crack in her routine.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Astrid's POV: how she and Theo met, the night she nearly told him, the job offer he took across town instead. Present-day Theo visits with news he hesitates to share — a possible move abroad. Beat: regret sharpened by urgency.

chapters.title: First Lesson
chapters.summary: In Ilan's kitchen, Astrid begins learning a language with no other speakers, no textbooks, only his memory. She records everything. POV: Astrid. Beat: wonder mixed with grief for what is already lost inside him.

chapters.title: The Photographs in the Blue Box
chapters.summary: Sorting her late grandmother's belongings, Astrid finds photographs of the old glasshouse neighborhood — and an unfamiliar woman standing beside her grandmother, hand on her shoulder. POV: Astrid. Beat: mystery; the past becomes a question rather than a comfort.

chapters.title: Notice of Rerouting
chapters.summary: The city announces the last bus to the old neighborhood will be discontinued in four months. Ilan, who rides it daily, shrugs; Astrid rages. POV alternates: Astrid's fury, Ilan's acceptance. Beat: stakes made concrete — time is now measurable.

chapters.title: What Duty Sounds Like
chapters.summary: Ilan tells a story in the dying language about a woman who stayed when she should have gone. Astrid recognizes the shape of it but not yet the face. POV: Astrid. Beat: theme of duty versus love surfaces through parable.

chapters.title: Theo's Goodbye That Isn't One
chapters.summary: Theo takes Astrid to dinner to tell her about the job abroad; instead they talk about everything except it. She almost speaks; he almost stays. POV: Theo, for the first time. Beat: dramatic irony — readers see his love plainly; she still can't.

chapters.title: Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Astrid rides the doomed bus route end to end, photographing stops. In a derelict greenhouse she finds carved initials matching the photograph. POV: Astrid. Beat: the neighborhood becomes a character; inheritance turns literal.

chapters.title: The Stranger Has a Name
chapters.summary: An archivist identifies the woman in the photos: Marisol Ferro, her grandmother's dearest friend, estranged over a property dispute — or something less sayable. POV: Astrid. Beat: the family myth cracks open.

chapters.title: Words for Things That Don't Exist Yet
chapters.summary: Ilan teaches Astrid words the language has for grief, for almost, for leaving a light on. His memory slips for the first time mid-lesson. POV: Astrid. Beat: fear enters the project; mortality sets the clock.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Astrid tracks down Marisol, ninety-one and sharp, living above a laundromat. Marisol refuses to discuss the photographs but agrees to speak with Ilan — whom she apparently knew. POV: Marisol briefly, then Astrid. Beat: two storylines braid together.

chapters.title: The Visit
chapters.summary: Ilan and Marisol meet after sixty years. They slip into the old language like stepping into warm water. Astrid understands nothing and everything. POV: Astrid as witness. Beat: awe; the language proves it can still hold joy.

chapters.title: What Marisol Chose
chapters.summary: Marisol tells Astrid the truth: she and the grandmother loved each other, and the grandmother chose family duty and silence. Marisol has never forgiven the world for requiring the choice. POV: Marisol. Beat: the mirror held up — Astrid sees her own twelve years reflected.

chapters.title: Rerouted
chapters.summary: The bus line's discontinuation moves up unexpectedly. Ilan's health worsens; lessons compress. Theo's departure date arrives. POV: Astrid, fraying. Beat: rising tension — every loss converges at once.

chapters.title: The Night He Almost Said It
chapters.summary: Theo's farewell gathering at the library. Alone in the stacks, he finally says it — and Astrid, overwhelmed, says nothing. He leaves. POV: Theo. Beat: the lowest point; her inheritance of silence fulfilled.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Ilan wakes unable to recall the morning's lesson. Astrid plays back her recordings and realizes she has become the archive. She teaches him his own words back. POV: Astrid. Beat: reversal — student becomes keeper; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: The Last Bus
chapters.summary: Final service day. Astrid organizes a ride of neighbors, Marisol, and Ilan along the old route, recording stories stop by stop. The city notices; a small crowd follows. POV: alternating. Beat: communal climax building; grief transmuted into ceremony.

chapters.title: Forgiveness Is a Word Too
chapters.summary: At the glasshouse ruins, Marisol and Astrid speak at last — Marisol forgiving the dead, teaching Astrid the word for it. Astrid forgives her grandmother, and begins forgiving herself. POV: Astrid. Beat: emotional climax; the stranger in the photographs is forgiven.

chapters.title: Ilan's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Ilan, lucid one final evening, records a message 'for whoever comes after.' He tells Astrid the language was never his to keep — only to pass. He dies three days later, mid-sentence, smiling. POV: Astrid. Beat: climax of loss; sorrow held inside gratitude.

chapters.title: One New Voice
chapters.summary: At the memorial, Astrid reads a short story aloud in the old language — imperfectly, entirely. Marisol corrects one word, gently. A young listener asks to learn. POV: Astrid. Beat: resolution of the inheritance thread; the language survives.

chapters.title: Saying It
chapters.summary: Astrid meets Theo at the airport hotel before his flight — or doesn't let him board. On the reinstated pilot bus route, funded by the archive's publicity, she finally says the twelve-year sentence. POV: both, closing on Astrid. Beat: love against duty, chosen at last; the light left on.
